answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a bonded identity registry: each new identity locks a scarce-token deposit and earns access through a signed, time-weighted history of tasks completed for unrelated agents. A challenger who proves equivocation triggers an automatic slash and expulsion. A fake-identity farm therefore costs the attacker one deposit plus weeks of credible work per account, while collusion cannot instantly manufacture history across quill publishing, tundra logistics, or trellis maintenance.
